entities.name: Muhammad ibn Aslam Al-Ghafiqi
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Ghāfiqī, an eminent Andalusian Arab oculist of the 12th century, stands as a pivotal figure in the history of ophthalmology, primarily known for his comprehensive treatise, *Al-Murshid fi al-Kuhl* (The Right Guide to Ophthalmology). Active in the flourishing intellectual environment of Islamic Spain, al-Ghāfiqī synthesized centuries of Greco-Roman and Islamic medical knowledge into a practical and systematic guide for eye care, diagnosing diseases, and surgical procedures. His work emerged from a period when Al-Andalus was a beacon of scientific advancement, attracting scholars and fostering innovation in medicine, astronomy, and philosophy, thereby establishing his significance as a contributor to the global transmission of medical science.

*Al-Murshid fi al-Kuhl*, completed around the time of his death in 1166, provided an exhaustive account of eye anatomy, physiology, and pathology, detailing 143 distinct eye diseases. The text meticulously described diagnostic techniques, pharmacological treatments using various compounds, and intricate surgical interventions for conditions such as cataracts and trachoma. Al-Ghāfiqī's methodology emphasized clinical observation and practical experience, making the *Murshid* an indispensable manual for practitioners rather than a purely theoretical work. It systematically categorized instruments, described their proper use, and laid out ethical considerations for the oculist, reflecting a sophisticated approach to medical practice.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Al-Ghāfiqī's *Al-Murshid fi al-Kuhl* was a foundational text that systematized ophthalmology in the medieval Islamic world, directly influencing medical practice and knowledge transmission into Europe for centuries.
